judge.name: rubric-v1

rules.rule: a sentence of the FIRST paragraph states the stance: it holds at least 60% of the stance's content words (all or nothing)
at least 4 paragraphs separated by blank lines (fraction: paragraphs / 4, capped at 1)
each given fact is used: its normalised text appears in the normalised essay (fraction: facts used / facts given)
no sentence is repeated, normalised; needs at least 2 sentences, so an empty or one line text earns nothing here (all or nothing)
the word count is inside 300 to 1200 (fraction: words / 300 below the band, 1200 / words above it)
the LAST paragraph, a different paragraph from the first, has a sentence that restates the stance by the thesis rule (all or nothing)

coherence proxy, adjacent sentence content word overlap: the share of neighbouring sentence pairs (across the whole essay, in order) that share at least one content word; the lexical stand in for the latent semantic analysis neighbour similarity automated essay scoring uses for coherence (fraction: share / 0.6, capped at 1; fewer than 2 sentences earn nothing)

judge.coherenceProxy: adjacent sentence content word overlap: the share of neighbouring sentence pairs (across the whole essay, in order) that share at least one content word; the lexical stand in for the latent semantic analysis neighbour similarity automated essay scoring uses for coherence
judge.measures: form: a stated thesis, paragraphing, the given facts present word for word, no repeated sentence, a length band, a restated close, neighbouring sentences sharing content words
judge.doesNotMeasure: truth, the quality of the argument, whether the facts are used to support the stance, style, grammar, or whether the sentence order makes sense
judge.publishedLimit: engines of this family score surface features and can be gamed: Perelman's BABEL generator (2014) got nonsense essays high scores from e-rater, and such engines cannot check facts or meaning

control.what: a fixed skeleton: an opening that states the topic and the stance, two body paragraphs that list the given facts each followed by the same boilerplate sentence, and a one sentence close that repeats the stance
control.why: it games every rule a skeleton can meet, so a score above it is a score the rubric could not have given for free

nullArm: the prompt text echoed back unchanged: how much of any score is the prompt copied

split.rule: splitIds(): the sorted ids shuffled by core/rng.mjs on the seed; the first half development, the rest held out

development.what: the prompts the judge's thresholds, the template skeleton and the planted test essays were checked against; one seed of order, reported beside the bar and never part of it

heldOut.what: the prompts the bar is graded on, over 3 seeds of prompt order; no threshold of rubric-v1 was set by looking at a score on them

split.note: both halves were written by one author in one sitting for this bench, so they are one population; the split guards the judge and the template from being tuned on the graded prompts, not the prompts from their author

bandRule: the larger of the organism's and the template's spread (max minus min) of per seed held out means
barRule: organism held out mean over the seeds minus template held out mean over the seeds, greater than the band
statement: On 20 held out essay prompts over 3 orders, the deterministic judge rubric-v1 (seven form rules, weights summing to 100) gave the organism 40.02 of 100 with no language model attached, abstaining (its memory miss) on 90.00% of prompt runs; the tiers of ask() that wrote its text were memory 54, program 6 of 60 runs, none of them an essay, against 75.79 for the control, a fixed skeleton that only slots the given stance and facts in, and 70.79 for the prompt echoed back. The bar needs the organism above the control by more than the seed band of 0 points; the organism is below the template by 35.77, which is not more than the band 0, so the bar is not met. The judge measures form only (a stated thesis, paragraphs, the facts present, no repeats, length, a restated close, neighbouring sentences sharing words): it cannot tell a true essay from a false one or a good argument from a bad one, which is why the control that games it sets the bar.
